transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, well, I came in because... it's my work, mostly. I'm an artist, and lately, my artist statements and the notes I send to clients, and even what I say in meetings... people keep telling me they can’t follow what I’m trying to explain. 

I guess I've started jumping around a lot? Like, I'll be talking about textures—which, actually, I just switched to this amazing raw linen canvas I found at a little shop on 4th street. The owner there has this giant orange cat that just sleeps on the receipt printer all day, it's so funny. And he sheds everywhere, but the linen absorbs oil paint so beautifully, so it's worth the trip. 

But yeah, I'll be explaining the textures to a gallery rep or a client, and then suddenly I'm talking about the project budgets, and then the secret meanings behind the brushstrokes, and... I don't know. People just look at me like I'm speaking another language and tell me they're completely lost.
Do you find yourself talking more quickly than usual or feeling like your thoughts are racing ahead of each other?

Um, yeah, definitely. It's like my brain is just... zooming. My thoughts can move so fast that images, exhibition titles, the language for this grant I'm applying for, colors, and just random conversations all stack on top of each other before I can even finish one idea. It gets really crowded up there. 

Actually, that reminds me of the grant I was looking at yesterday for local creatives. The website was so incredibly outdated, like early 2000s HTML, with those awful neon blue hyperlinks? I almost emailed the webmaster to offer to redesign it, because honestly, a good layout makes such a difference when you're trying to showcase art. I learned a bit of coding back in college when I took this interactive media elective. My professor for that class had the most amazing collection of vintage typewriters in his office. I've always wanted to incorporate typewriter keys into a mixed media piece... 

Wait, sorry. Did that answer your question? I know you asked about my thoughts racing. But yeah, everything just piles up all at once.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like needing less sleep or feeling rested with only a few hours of sleep?

Yeah, actually, I haven't really been needing much sleep at all. I'll be working super late in the studio, and then I can just sleep for maybe two or three hours and wake up feeling totally bright and ready to keep going. I'm not tired the way I normally would be, which is honestly great for my productivity. 

Like, the other night I was up at 3 AM working on this large-scale piece, and the lighting in my studio is just so different at that hour. The streetlights outside cast this weird amber glow through the blinds, and there was this huge moth just throwing itself against the window glass. It had these incredible fuzzy antennae. I actually stopped painting the canvas and started sketching the moth on a scrap piece of cardboard I had from a delivery box. I get all my heavy supplies delivered now because the local store doesn't carry the specific brand of cadmium red I like. Cadmium red is such a gorgeous color but it's so toxic, you have to be super careful with it. A friend of mine in undergrad actually got sick because she used to point her brushes with her lips, which is just... a terrible habit. I always use a rag. I have this whole pile of rags that used to be my old band t-shirts... 

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, sleep. Right. But yeah, just two or three hours and I'm completely energized and ready to go again.
Have you noticed that your mood has been unusually high, excited, or euphoric lately?

Um, yeah, I'd say so. For stretches, I just feel completely lit up, you know? Like I'm almost unstoppable and every single idea I have is just brilliant. It's an amazing feeling, honestly. But then, on the flip side, someone—like a collaborator or a client—will make just a tiny comment about my work, and I'll just snap. Like, I get so irritable and my reaction feels way bigger than whatever they actually said. 

Which is really frustrating because I try so hard to maintain good relationships with the people I work with. Like this one gallery owner I was talking to last week, she has this incredible space downtown with these huge exposed brick walls. I love exposed brick, it adds such a nice warmth to a room. My first apartment out of college had an exposed brick wall in the kitchen, but the grout was always crumbling into my coffee maker. I had this little cheap drip coffee maker that I bought at a thrift store for like, three dollars. The thrift store was right next to this amazing bakery that made the best almond croissants. I used to go there every Sunday morning and just sit by the window and sketch people walking by. I saw this guy once walking a pig on a leash. A literal pig! It was wearing a tiny red harness and everything...

But yeah, my mood. It's either super high and excited, or I'm just snapping at people over nothing.

Have you ever had a period of time when you felt down or depressed most of the day, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, or experienced changes in your appetite or concentration for at least two weeks?

No, not really. I don't think I've ever felt like that for two weeks straight. Sometimes I'll get a little bummed out if a piece isn't coming together, but I don't just lose interest in everything. I'm usually pretty driven to keep making things. 

Actually, I did have a bit of a slump last month when my favorite art supply store closed down. It was this independent place that had been there for like, thirty years. The owner, this guy named Arthur, knew exactly what kind of charcoal I liked. He had this enormous gray cat that just slept on the counter all day. I'm pretty sure it was a Maine Coon, it was massive. My cousin has a Maine Coon, and she actually trained it to walk on a leash, kind of like that pig I saw! She takes it to the farmer's market on Saturdays. I love the farmer's market, especially in the late summer when all the heirloom tomatoes are out. The colors of heirloom tomatoes are just unbelievable—those deep purples and striped greens. I tried to mix a paint color to match this one Cherokee Purple tomato I bought, but getting that exact earthy, bruised purple tone is so tricky. You have to use just a tiny touch of raw umber... 

Oh, wait, you asked about being depressed, right? No, I haven't really had anything like that. Just the normal ups and downs, but definitely not for weeks at a time.
Have you had a period of at least a few days to a week where your mood was so high, irritable, or energized that it was clearly different from your usual self and noticeable to others?

Yeah, definitely. It's been going on for a while now, actually. I'd say those stretches where I'm just totally energized, snapping at people, barely sleeping but juggling a million projects... that's been happening for about ten months now. 

It really started right around the time I was trying to put together a portfolio for this residency program in Berlin. Berlin has such an incredible art scene, especially the street art. I follow this one collective on Instagram that does these massive, intricate wheat-paste murals on abandoned buildings in East Berlin. Wheat-pasting is such a cool technique, but it's so messy. I tried it once in my studio and ended up gluing a piece of newsprint to my favorite pair of jeans. They were these vintage Levi's I found at a flea market, the kind with the button fly instead of a zipper. I always prefer button flies, they just feel more authentic, you know? The guy who sold them to me had this whole booth dedicated to just denim and old brass belt buckles. He was wearing a hat made out of recycled tire rubber, which I thought was so innovative. People are doing such amazing things with upcycled materials these days...

But yeah, to answer your question, those high and irritable periods have been a thing for about ten months.

The lack of depressive symptoms rules out Bipolar II and Major Depressive Disorder. No features of psychosis or other disorders were endorsed. F31.9 (Bipolar Disorder, unspecified) remains the most appropriate code based on current information.
